contributions.statement: Do not pre-inject retrieved candidate files into a coding agent's prompt unless the retriever's file precision is high (≥~0.65 here). BM25-grade candidates (precision ~0.38) acted as distractors, raising tokens on jointly-solved issues by ~39% and slightly lowering resolve rate.
contributions.evidence: Tables 2-3, §5.1: BM25 0.375 precision → −0.6 pp, +21% resolved tokens (+38.6% on 94 paired instances); Jina 0.445 neutral; CodeGrep 0.677 −15% paired tokens. One agent, one run.

contributions.statement: When comparing agent configurations on cost, report rounds/tokens on the instances both configurations resolve, not each configuration's own resolved set; here pooling overstated token savings by about a quarter.
contributions.evidence: §5.3: pooled −19% tokens vs paired −15% (96 jointly resolved instances); rounds −15% pooled vs −9% paired.
relative_to: paired comparison / survivorship control in evaluation

contributions.statement: Better file localization mostly shortens rollouts rather than raising resolve rate; failures on unsolved issues sit in patch synthesis, not in finding files.
contributions.evidence: §5.1: v2→v3 +28% median Fβ yields +0.4 pp resolve but −12% tokens; mechanism asserted, not measured by failure annotation.

reason: The precision-threshold anti-pattern qualifies: paired-instance evidence that low-precision context injection costs tokens. That matters for any graph or index tool that pushes candidates into context. Resolve-rate claims are within noise, and the paper does not support 'small explorer, frontier solves'.
